clue.text: Articles of feminine make-up

parts.note: not cosmetics at all: the nursery rhyme lists what little girls are made of

explanation.surface: A list of cosmetics in a woman's handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests lipstick and powder; the rhyme 'What are little girls made of?' answers with these ingredients, and 'everything nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: The old nursery rhyme says girls are made of these ingredients, so they are literally the components of femininity.

clue.text: Wise "pacifists" their inhabitanis?

parts.note: pacifists is read as Pacific-ists, people of the Pacific, living on islands named after the wise biblical king

explanation.surface: A question about where sensible peace-lovers live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pacifists' is in quotes because it means natives of the Pacific, not peace campaigners; Solomon is the proverbially wise king of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific archipelago east of New Guinea bears the name of the wise king of the Bible.

clue.text: Note town in Bucks conspicuous at the present time

parts.note: G is a musical note
Iver is a village in Buckinghamshire, near Slough

explanation.surface: A remark that a Buckinghamshire town is prominent nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is Buckinghamshire, an English county. 'The present time' is not now but the time of presents, Christmas, when a donor stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hands out gifts is prominent at Christmas, a season of presents.

clue.text: Concerning something golden, including one characteristic of Tigger

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the golden thing takes the numeral within it

parts.note: the proverb says silence is golden
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remark about something golden that shows one of Tigger's traits.
explanation.walkthrough: Tigger is the endlessly bouncy tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger is famously bouncy, and springiness is the ability to bounce back.

clue.text: Simple folk landing in the soup!

explanation.surface: Naive people getting themselves into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' sounds like being in trouble, but it is literal: pasta strands floating in broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly people are called this informally, and the pasta strands are a common soup ingredient.

clue.text: Cast over head to show some diffidence

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Throwing something over one's head out of bashfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity and reserve, a lack of confidence, are the same quality as diffidence.

clue.text: The island is absorbed in nationalism

indicators.note: the island's name sits soaked up inside the letters of the word nationalism

explanation.surface: A small island swept up in a nationalist movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebridean island off Mull, where St Columba founded his monastery.

clue.text: Ash Wednesday is not one of these

definitions.text: Ash Wednesday is not one of these

parts.words: Ash Wednesday is not one of these
parts.note: ash suggests the remains of a fire, but the church's quarterly fast days are a separate observance

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's note that the start of Lent belongs to another category.
explanation.walkthrough: The four sets of quarterly fast days fall on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday; one set follows Ash Wednesday, which is not itself among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The quarterly fasting days of the Western church sound as if ash should belong to them, but it does not.

clue.text: Capital building material on the Continent

definitions.text: Capital building material on the Continent

parts.words: Capital building material on the Continent
parts.note: capital means both excellent and belonging to a European capital city

explanation.surface: A fine construction material found in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The gypsum-based setting powder takes its name from the French capital.

clue.text: Is devoted to the right type of Romance literature

parts.note: someone devoted to a thing loves it
a Tory belongs to the political right in Britain

explanation.surface: A reader with conservative tastes who adores a particular kind of romantic fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party, the right wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic novel centred on a courtship is a familiar genre of fiction.

clue.text: No idol, he, promoting peace etc

parts.note: taken as written
Bel is the Babylonian god worshipped as an idol in the Apocrypha's story of Bel and the Dragon

explanation.surface: A man who worships no false god and campaigns for peace and other good causes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the Swedish industrialist whose will founded the prizes for peace, literature, physics and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, the dynamite inventor, endowed annual prizes for peace and other achievements.

clue.text: The subject of this painting could be wallflowers

definitions.text: The subject of this painting could be wallflowers

parts.words: The subject of this painting could be wallflowers
parts.note: wallflowers here are not shy dancers or garden plants but any flowers painted straight onto a wall

explanation.surface: An art critic suggesting a picture shows garden plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting done directly on a wall surface would show, quite literally, flowers on a wall.

clue.text: Foreigner lacks a legal right

indicators.note: the foreigner lacks the word a, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: An immigrant without some entitlement under the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal claim held over another's property until a debt is settled.

clue.text: Just the woman to show the flag

explanation.surface: Only a certain woman can raise the banner.
explanation.walkthrough: A flag is also a wild plant with sword-shaped leaves, the yellow flag; 'the woman' asks for a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and a plant of the genus whose common wild species is called the yellow flag.

clue.text: They are in the following category

definitions.text: They are in the following category

parts.words: They are in the following category
parts.note: the following is not the next item in a list but those who follow on after someone

explanation.surface: A pointer to the next item in a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs and replacements come after, or follow, their predecessors.

clue.text: For paying lump sums in gold?

definitions.text: For paying lump sums in gold?

parts.words: For paying lump sums in gold?
parts.note: lump sums are read literally as lumps of gold handed over as payment

explanation.surface: A question about settling a large payment in bullion.
explanation.definitionFit: Small lumps of native gold found by prospectors could be used as currency.

clue.text: Caprine quality seems to make .the world go round?

definitions.text: seems to make .the world go round?

explanation.surface: A goat-like trait that apparently keeps the planet spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: Caprine means goat-like: to play the giddy goat is to act frivolously. Dizziness also makes the room seem to spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Frivolity like a skittish goat's, and dizziness, the feeling that everything spins.

clue.text: Food custom in South Africa

parts.note: usage is custom or habitual practice

explanation.surface: A culinary tradition in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In these old Times puzzles 'Food' can stand alone as a definition: any item eaten counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger, a minced-meat link in a skin, is an item of food.

clue.text: Conveyance .for one passenger rather than a team

definitions.text: Conveyance .for one passenger rather than a team

parts.words: Conveyance .for one passenger rather than a team
parts.note: a side is a team, so this vehicle carries one passenger where a team would need more

explanation.surface: A transport option for a single traveller instead of a whole squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcycle attachment carries just one passenger beside the rider.

clue.text: Do a good turn — book into Dream of Paris

indicators.note: the book goes into the French dream

parts.note: reve is French for dream
vol is the abbreviation for volume, a book

explanation.surface: Be helpful by slipping a novel into a Parisian fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good turn' is not a favour but a full rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate fully is literally to make a complete turn.

clue.text: Artist's cap is so eccentric

definitions.note: read as 'Artist is', the 's being a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: something eccentric is odd and off-centre, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A painter's hat is rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CAP IS SO, signalled by 'eccentric', gives the Spanish painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo, the Spanish co-founder of Cubism, is one of the most famous painters.

clue.text: One should be sorry to do this

definitions.text: One should be sorry to do this

parts.words: One should be sorry to do this
parts.note: not a regret about some act but the act of atonement a contrite person performs

explanation.surface: A warning against some regrettable act.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of atonement are done by someone repentant, out of sorrow for a sin.

clue.text: The eastern half of Disney's musical pot-pourri

indicators.note: of means the answer is taken out of the film's title, its later half once the opening letters go

parts.note: Fantasia is Disney's 1940 film, a medley of animated classical pieces

explanation.surface: A remark about the second part of an animated film set to classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'The eastern half' is the continent; read with 'of', it also says which half of FANTASIA is kept: drop FANT and the eastern, right-hand half remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent stretching east from Europe is loosely the eastern half of the world.

clue.text: Name of one preceding the vehicle

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other, so the numeral leads and the vehicle follows it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone's name painted on the front of a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian man's first name, the equivalent of John.

clue.text: This vessel may return to still waters

indicators.note: returning means the word for still waters is read backwards

parts.note: pools are bodies of still water

explanation.surface: A boat that might come back to a calm harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted sailing boat is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Animal in a pound

explanation.surface: A stray creature held in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like an animal enclosure, but it is the weight: sixteen of these make one pound. The animal is the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, and a weight of which sixteen make up the avoirdupois pound.

clue.text: Sign at Castle Adamant?

parts.note: the castle in Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida bars all men, so its notice would announce their exclusion

explanation.surface: A question about a notice at a stern fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: In Princess Ida, men are barred from the women's university at Castle Adamant, so the notice would read 'no men', written as O (nothing) plus MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign, and the letters split as nought and men, the castle's rule.

clue.text: Lamb wrote of such children

parts.note: Charles Lamb, the English essayist: A Reverie' about the imagined children he never had

explanation.surface: A literary question about the kind of children an author described.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamb is not a baby sheep but Charles Lamb, whose Essays of Elia include this piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb's essay title calls the imaginary children of his reverie by this word.

clue.text: He has certainly gained ground

parts.note: gaining ground usually means making progress; here it means literally acquiring land

explanation.surface: A man who has undoubtedly made progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who possesses an estate has, quite literally, acquired land.

clue.text: The folly of getting knocked out

explanation.surface: The foolishness of a boxer who ends up flat on the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of senseless: foolish and pointless, or unconscious after a blow.
